evidence.excerpt: GATK HaplotypeCaller remains a bottleneck in clinical WES pipelines because its local de novo assembly step is largely single-threaded at the per-sample level. We systematically evaluated three strategies for throughput improvement on a cohort of 412 anonymised WES samples (mean coverage 85×, 38–62 Mb target): genomic-interval scatter–gather with 100 Mb shards, sample-level parallelism across nodes, and a combination of both. Job orchestration used Snakemake with a SLURM backend. The scatter–gather approach alone reduced mean per-sample runtime from 4.1 hours to 41 minutes on 32 cores. Combining it with sample-level parallelism across 8 nodes processed the full 412-sample cohort in 19 hours wall time compared to 70 hours in the sequential baseline. We measured concordance against the baseline using precision and recall on GIAB benchmark variants: SNP precision 99.91 %, recall 99.87 %; indel precision 99.34 %, recall 99.21 %. Configuration files and Snakemake rules are provided as supplementary material.
